summary: Discovery call to understand Zephyr's current vector search architecture and evaluate Redwood Hosted/Dedicated/Private for embeddings + reranking. Key concerns: throughput at 500 qps, dimensionality choice, hybrid BM25+vector rerank, and data residency/security for EU customers. Agreed to run a short benchmark and share pricing/security docs.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Alex from Redwood. Priya is on the call too. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Sam: Good, thanks. Sam here. We've been running a couple of experiments with embeddings for our search rerank, want to see what Redwood offers.
[00:12] Maya: Hi, Maya. We lead the eng team working on search.
[00:16] Jordan: Jordan, data science. Hi all.
[00:20] Priya: Great — quick agenda: we're going to ask about your current stack, desired SLOs, and then go into options (hosted vs dedicated vs private). We'll touch on vector DB integration, throughput, and hybrid search patterns.
[00:35] Sam: Sounds good. Quick background: we have a Postgres-backed product catalog, currently using BM25 for initial retrieval, then a small re-ranker using OpenAI embeddings + cosine similarity stored in Pinecone. It's getting costly and latency is spiky — p95 is around 700ms for rerank right now.
[00:55] Alex: Got it. So your pipeline is BM25 -> embeddings similarity in Pinecone -> rerank?
[00:59] Jordan: Yeah. We compute 512-d embeddings with a finetuned model, store them in Pinecone, run top-200 then rerank with a cross-encoder locally.
[01:12] Priya: When you say 512-d, is that fixed? Are you open to trying 384 or 256 for perf/cost tradeoffs?
[01:20] Jordan: We're using a legacy 512 from the finetune. We can try lower dims if accuracy holds. Our 95% of traffic is simple queries but we have bursts to 500 qps during business hours.
[01:32] Maya: Important for us: some customers in EU require data residency and stricter controls, so we need either region controls or private deployment.
[01:40] Alex: Totally. Redwood offers Hosted with region controls, Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput, and Private (VPC/on-prem) for stricter residency and network controls. For the throughput you mentioned — bursts to 500 qps — Dedicated is a common fit.
[01:56] Sam: Can the hosted API sustain 500 qps for rerank with 200 candidates?
[02:02] Priya: It depends on the model choices and batching. For pure vector similarity at top-k we can handle a lot, but if your rerank is a cross-encoder that scores pairs, that's more expensive. Two options we often see: 1) do vector search to get top-N then a lightweight reranker (bi-encoder or small cross-encoder) on Redwood Dedicated or 2) offload extremely expensive cross-encoder to a separate pool and use fallback policies.
[02:27] Jordan: Our current cross-encoder is fairly heavy. The plan was to move the bi-encoder stage to embeddings and do a small cross-encoder only for top-50.
[02:36] Alex: That's sensible. Also want to flag hybrid search: BM25 for recall then vector rerank is common; Redwood supports hybrid workflows and can integrate with external vector DBs or host embeddings itself. Are you married to Pinecone?
[02:50] Sam: Not married, but switching is non-trivial. We like Pinecone's ops model.
[02:55] Priya: Integrations we offer: we can pull vectors from your existing DB via connector, or we can host embeddings and the index on Redwood Dedicated. If you keep Pinecone, we can call it as a pre-step and then do rerank on Redwood. There may be added network latencies.
[03:10] Maya: What's the typical p95 we should expect if we move both vector store and rerank to Redwood Dedicated?
[03:16] Priya: Rough numbers: for a bi-encoder retrieval+rerank flow on Dedicated, p95 in the 100-200ms range is achievable for top-50 reranks, depending on vector dimensionality and batch config. For heavy cross-encoders maybe 250-400ms. Those are ballpark and we'll need to benchmark with your data.
[03:33] Jordan: About dimensionality — if we switch to 384 from 512 do you see big recall drop?
[03:38] Priya: Usually small — many modern embedding models use 384 or 512; 256 is sometimes ok but depends on training. We recommend experiments. Also quantization can change memory and throughput tradeoffs.
[03:50] Sam: We have concerns about export controls and encryption—some customers want BYOK and HSM support.
[03:57] Alex: Redwood Private supports KMS integrations and HSM for key management, plus audit logs and SOC2. For hosted customers we have SOC2 controls and key management options; Dedicated can be provisioned with customer-managed VPC peering for better control.
[04:12] Maya: For private deployment, do you offer on-prem or only VPC?
[04:16] Alex: We offer both: private VPC deployments in customer cloud and an on-prem package for air-gapped requirements. The private control plane can sit in your account for compliance.
[04:25] Sam: Would that raise the cost materially?
[04:28] Alex: Private has a higher baseline due to support and infra packaging. Dedicated is more predictable — reserved monthly commit — with lower variability than hosted usage billing. We'll send estimates in the pricing doc.
[04:40] Jordan: For the rerank candidate size: we tend to fetch 200 candidates from vector DB then rerank to top 10. Is there a mode where Redwood does approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) + rerank inline to avoid extra hops?
[04:53] Priya: Yes — Redwood can host the ANN index and perform a single integrated flow: nearest neighbor retrieval followed by rerank. That reduces network hops and can lower latency. If you host vectors externally, then it's an extra round-trip.
[05:05] Sam: How about cost? Is hosting vectors with Redwood cheaper than Pinecone at scale?
[05:10] Alex: Cost comparisons vary. For high QPS and large vector counts, Dedicated with optimized quantization and batching is often more cost-effective. We'll run a TCO estimate based on your numbers.
[05:22] Maya: Security checklist — SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, EU data residency, SOC2/ISO — do you have a security packet?
[05:30] Alex: Yes, we'll share our security brief and SOC2 report. Priya can add architecture notes on network controls.
[05:36] Priya: One technical question: what's your vector index size? How many vectors and average dims?
[05:41] Jordan: About 12 million product vectors at 512 dims, growth of ~200k/month. Most queries require top-50.
[05:48] Priya: 12M is fine; quantization and sharding decisions will affect latency. For example, going to 384 or using 8-bit quant gives memory savings and faster inference on GPU.
[05:58] Sam: For inference models, do you recommend open models or proprietary? We currently use a finetuned OpenAI embedder.
[06:05] Alex: We support a variety. Open models can reduce cost and give control. If you need high fidelity finetuned embeddings, it's possible to host your model on Dedicated or Private with Redwood. There's a tradeoff: hosted open models for lower cost, private/fine-tuned models for better control and potentially higher accuracy.
[06:24] Jordan: Latency SLO: we want p95 < 300ms for rerank during normal load and graceful degradation to 500ms under burst. Is that realistic?
[06:32] Priya: Yes, with Dedicated and optimized batch sizes. We'll want to test under your realistic query mix. We'll propose a benchmark that measures throughput vs recall and p95.
[06:40] Sam: For hybrid BM25 + vector rerank, how do you suggest we orchestrate the two? Keep BM25 in Postgres and call Redwood for embeddings?
[06:48] Priya: Two approaches: 1) Keep BM25 in Postgres and do an async call to Redwood for vector rerank — but that adds latency. 2) Push BM25 first-step to a lightweight retrieval on your side, then send candidate set to Redwood for rerank — that's what you're doing now. Another option is to centralize retrieval on Redwood if you migrate the index.
[07:05] Maya: We're also tracking cost per query — want to keep it under $0.004/query across retrieval+rerank ideally.
[07:12] Alex: We'll include cost projections. There's often a sweet spot with lower-dim embeddings and small cross-encoder budget to hit cost targets.
[07:20] Jordan: On the topic of batching — does Redwood do automatic request batching for embeddings/rerank?
[07:25] Priya: Yes, the runtime does continuous batching and KV cache optimizations. For embeddings generation we batch requests; for rerank we can batch smaller groups depending on latency SLO. We'll tune batch windows per route.
[07:36] Sam: Any limits on dimension sizes or vector DB formats for import?
[07:40] Priya: We support common vector formats (float32, int8 quantized) and typical dims. If you have large bulk imports we'll assist with migration tools and streaming ingestion.
[07:50] Maya: What's the onboarding timeline for a Dedicated deployment?
[07:54] Alex: Typical onboard to Dedicated is 4–6 weeks for a standard deployment with reserved capacity; Private on-prem takes longer depending on infra. We can shorten for pilots.
[08:02] Jordan: For the benchmark, what metrics will you need from us?
[08:06] Priya: Sample vectors (100k), query logs (a week), desired recall/quality targets, current latency measurements. We'll provide a script to run locally and an S3 path spec.
[08:18] Sam: About the rerank model — if we want to keep the cross-encoder in-house for IP reasons, can Redwood call out to our service during reranks?
[08:26] Priya: You can either host the cross-encoder in your private deployment or call out over network to your model if you allow the latency. Many customers host the heavy model in their VPC and Redwood orchestrates.
[08:40] Maya: Any common gotchas?
[08:42] Priya: Watch out for candidate set sizes (fetching 2k then reranking is usually overkill), and shuffle in embeddings (make sure all vectors are normalized and consistent). Also watch tokenization differences if you generate embeddings from different models.
[08:56] Jordan: Our recall@10 is about 0.78 currently. Target is >0.82.
[09:00] Alex: Great target. Often we tune embedding model, candidate size, and reranker to hit that.
[09:06] Sam: Let's talk logistics — can you share a pricing snapshot soon?
[09:09] Alex: Yes — I'll send hosted vs dedicated TCO and an estimate for a private deployment.
[09:14] Maya: Also need the SOC2 and data residency docs.
[09:17] Alex: We'll share the security packet after the call.
[09:20] Priya: For the benchmark, I'll draft the plan and include expected infra for a 1-week run at 500 qps peak with ramp.
[09:28] Jordan: One more question — do you have support for hybrid search combining BM25 scores with vector distance in a single ranking function?
[09:35] Priya: Yes — we support score blending where BM25/logits and vector similarity are combined. You can tune weights and run A/B.
[09:43] Sam: OK cool. That answers a lot.
[09:46] Alex: Quick recap of next steps: Alex will send pricing and security packet; Priya will share benchmark plan; Jordan will send sample data/query logs; and we'll schedule a follow-up architecture/benchmarks call.
[09:58] Maya: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[10:00] Sam: Thanks.
[10:04] Alex: Appreciate your time. We'll follow up by Friday.
[10:08] (call ends)

Note: transcription includes occasional mis-heard tokens (e.g., K V cache transcribed as K V cash) and speaker overlaps.
